lu-2Qmq.title: Sign: yellow framed direction signs
lu-2Qmq.summary: Yellow direction signs with a thin black outline, a pointed tip and a full frame around them. Town names are in capitals. Road numbers sit in a red box (1-2 digits) or a yellow box (3 digits).

lu-90cv.title: Bollard: black and white wedge
lu-90cv.summary: Black and white wedge-shaped bollard with a grey reflector, sometimes with an indent in the lower half. Looks like the German one, but the reflector has three bolts instead of two.

differs.how: German reflector has two bolts, not three

lu-D1t5.title: Signpost: bulky blue-and-white round reflector
lu-D1t5.summary: Some signposts carry a bulky round reflector with blue and white markings. Sweden and Finland have similar ones, but the landscape tells them apart.

lu-DmBj.title: Chevron: black with yellow arrows
lu-DmBj.summary: Black chevron boards with yellow arrows, rarely blue and yellow. No neighbour uses these, so it points to Luxembourg unless the landscape says Iceland, Norway, Finland, Ireland or Portugal.

differs.how: Same colours but a very different landscape
Same colours but a very different landscape

lu-F5fO.title: Landscape: vineyards in the southeast
lu-F5fO.summary: Vineyards are mostly in the southeast of the country.

lu-MrJA.title: Language: French most, then German
lu-MrJA.summary: Three official languages, but French is used most on road signs and adverts. German on signs is less common, though not rare.

lu-S1pq.title: Road numbers: 3 digits, first digit by area
lu-S1pq.summary: Local road numbers have three digits starting with 1 in the south, 2 around the capital and 3 in the north.

lu-SRxb.title: Houses: dark slate roofs, plain walls
lu-SRxb.summary: Houses have dark slate roofs and plain walls painted white, grey or pastel. Neighbouring parts of Belgium and France look the same, though it is most common here.

lu-YP0t.title: Landscape: green rolling hills
lu-YP0t.summary: Nearly everywhere is green rolling hills with a patchwork of farmland and forest. If you see yellow plates and are unsure, hills rule out the Netherlands, which is flat.

lu-aRna.title: Plate: long yellow with blue strip on left
lu-aRna.summary: Long yellow plates with a blue strip on the left. Foreign cars with white plates are fairly common because the country is small.

differs.how: Dutch plates are yellow front and rear, no blue strip
British plates are yellow only at the rear

lu-b7NW.title: Sign: pedestrian crossing, 5 vertical stripes
lu-b7NW.summary: The pedestrian crossing sign shows 5 vertical stripes. Belgian ones have 2 horizontal stripes.

lu-e5yT.title: Street sign: short, white, slanted blue corners
lu-e5yT.summary: Street name signs are short and mostly white, with designs varying by town. A common one has slanted blue corners.

differs.how: Belgian ones are also short but can be other colours
Dutch ones are blue, long and low

lu-gJw2.title: Sign: yellow framed town entrance
lu-gJw2.summary: Town entrance signs are yellow with a frame around them, usually with the town name in two languages. The road number and a speed limit often sit on top.

lu-jlnY.title: Language: German-looking with doubled vowels
lu-jlnY.summary: Looks like German, with umlauts, lots of double vowels and sometimes an accented é. Most town names come from Luxembourgish, German, or both.

lu-kWxo.title: Sign: white signposts
lu-kWxo.summary: Almost all road signs are mounted on white signposts. France has some too, but much less often.

lu-nKRO.title: Pole: upside-down trident top
lu-nKRO.summary: The most common pole has a top shaped like an upside-down trident, with other tops mixed in. France, Spain and Portugal have it too.

lu-oEEg.title: Landscape: hillier, higher north
lu-oEEg.summary: The north is hillier and higher than the south.

lu-oSnE.title: Road signs: square-cornered frames
lu-oSnE.summary: Frames like those on the direction signs appear on lots of other road items. Denmark has similar frames, but its corners are rounder, while these are more square.

differs.how: Danish frame corners are more rounded

lu-t9UN.title: Coverage: Gen 2 or Gen 4 camera
lu-t9UN.summary: Nearly all coverage is from the Gen 2 or Gen 4 camera. The older, blurrier Gen 3 exists but is rare.

lu-wuhb.title: Google car: Gen 3 backpack in city centre
lu-wuhb.summary: Parts of the capital's downtown were shot with a Gen 3 backpack camera. Sometimes you can see the carrier's sunglasses and greying hair.

lu-yx10.title: Sign: blue bus stop, bus with six windows
lu-yx10.summary: Bus stop signs are blue and always the same design, with a bus that has six windows. Belgian and Dutch ones look quite different; the Belgian one has a yellow post.

differs.how: Belgian bus stop sign has a different design and yellow post
Dutch bus stop sign has a different design
